findings.title: --format help text on diff does not warn that sarif is unavailable on DIFF kind while compat subcommands list sarif as built-in
findings.principle: Help text that hides invocation shape
findings.detail: The diff --format help says Built-in: human, json, junit which is accurate for FormatterKind.DIFF. The compat family says Built-in: human, json, junit, sarif which is accurate for COMPAT/COMPAT_HISTORY/COMPAT_BISECT. An agent that reads check --help first will cache {human,json,junit,sarif} as the valid set and attempt protokit diff --format sarif, receiving exit 2. The available-list in the error correctly shows only the DIFF-kind names, but the agent wastes one retry. No per-subcommand qualifier in any help text explains that sarif is compat-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parenthetical to the diff --format help: Built-in: human, json, junit (sarif not available on diff). Use --formatter-module to add more. One-line change to the help= kwarg at message/cli.py ~line 199.

findings.title: Built-in shadowing error wrapped under generic load-failure prefix indistinguishable from import errors for agent pattern-matching
findings.detail: When a pack tries to shadow a built-in (e.g. COMPAT json), register_formatter raises FormatterError. load_formatter_packs catches AttributeError TypeError and FormatterError together under error_exit(failed to load formatter pack name: exc). The verbatim exception text is present but an agent pattern-matching on failed to load will retry with a corrected module path rather than renaming the formatter. This is the --formatter-module my.module --format json where my.module defines (COMPAT json) scenario from the review intent.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the except clause into two blocks. Keep (AttributeError, TypeError) under failed to load formatter pack. Add a separate except FormatterError block emitting error_exit(f"formatter pack {name!r} conflicts with a reserved built-in name: {exc}"). Two distinct prefixes let agents branch without parsing embedded exception text.

findings.title: --formatter-module help omits that kind must be a FormatterKind enum instance not a string -- highest-friction failure mode for code-generating agents
findings.principle: Help text that hides invocation shape
findings.location: src/protokit/message/cli.py lines 203-206; src/protokit/schema/cli.py --formatter-module on all four subcommands
findings.detail: Help says Python module exposing a FORMATTERS list of (name, fn, kind) tuples. It does not state that kind must be a FormatterKind enum instance from protokit.formatters. An agent will use kind=DIFF (string) and receive TypeError: formatter pack: kind must be FormatterKind got str. The error is accurate but the help provides no hint a specific import is required.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend help to: Python module exposing FORMATTERS = [(name, fn, FormatterKind.X), ...]. Import FormatterKind from protokit.formatters. Repeatable. One-line help= kwarg update on each subcommand carrying --formatter-module.

findings.title: No TTY auto-detection -- agents must always pass --format explicitly or receive ANSI-colored output on every piped invocation
findings.location: All subcommands: message/cli.py and schema/cli.py --format options
findings.detail: Every subcommand defaults --format to human unconditionally. When piped, agents receive ANSI-colored text with click.style() escapes and Unicode characters. No PROTOKIT_FORMAT env var exists, no --format=auto mode, no isatty() check. The click.Choice -> click.STRING change was an extension point but did not add TTY awareness.
findings.suggested_fix: Add envvar=PROTOKIT_FORMAT to each --format Click option definition. Zero behavior change for interactive users; CI environments set the variable once. Alternatively resolve output_format in the command body: output_format = output_format or (human if sys.stdout.isatty() else json).

findings.title: stdout-write guard (redirect_stdout) does not intercept fd-level writes -- error message implies total protection it cannot deliver
findings.detail: contextlib.redirect_stdout rebinds sys.stdout. A formatter using os.write(1, b"leak") or print(file=sys.__stdout__) bypasses the capture. Leaked bytes corrupt the agent pipe without triggering the guard. The error message wrote to stdout directly implies full stdout capture which misleads formatter authors.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the error message to: formatter wrote to sys.stdout directly (low-level fd writes are not intercepted); formatters must return str only. Accuracy fix only. A complete guard requires dup2/pipe at OS fd level which is out of scope.

findings.title: check calls reject_quiet_plus_structured twice (direct + via _resolve_common_flags) while history/bisect call it once -- inconsistent validation order
findings.location: src/protokit/schema/cli.py: check() ~line 827 direct call vs _resolve_common_flags() which also calls reject_quiet_plus_structured
findings.detail: check() calls load_formatter_packs then reject_quiet_plus_structured directly then _resolve_common_flags which calls it again. For history/bisect, _resolve_common_flags contains the single call. Double-call is harmless today but creates inconsistent error-sequencing: on check, quiet+format validation fires before type resolution; on history/bisect it fires inside _resolve_common_flags after type flags are parsed. If the guard is ever changed to warn rather than hard-exit, check emits a duplicate warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the standalone reject_quiet_plus_structured call from check() body (diff line 827 in schema/cli.py). The call inside _resolve_common_flags is sufficient and makes all four subcommands consistent.

residual_risks.description: Formatter exception message suppresses tracebacks. If a formatter raises with empty str representation, agent receives formatter raised MyError: with trailing empty string -- exits 2 correctly but empty suffix may confuse parsers splitting on colon-space.

load_formatter_pack does not report which of the earlier-staged entries were rolled back on partial commit failure. Agent running a 5-formatter pack where the 4th collides receives only the error for the 4th with no list of the 3 rolled-back entries.

testing_gaps.description: No test exercises protokit diff --format sarif to confirm it exits 2 with the DIFF-kind available-list (human, json, junit) not the COMPAT list. Registry wiring bug where DIFF inherits COMPAT sarif would pass all existing tests.

No CLI-level test for --formatter-module my.pack --format json where my.pack defines (COMPAT, json) built-in collision. Should assert exit 2 and stderr contains built-in or reserved distinguishing it from import error.

No test verifies protokit compat check --quiet --format junit emits exactly one error line on stderr not two due to CR-06 double reject call. Needed to catch regressions if guard is changed from error_exit to soft warning.
